identity.description: Convex blend of L1 and L2 penalties: keeps lasso's exact-zero selection while the L2 component adds the grouping effect — correlated features enter and leave the support TOGETHER instead of lasso's arbitrary single pick. The default when you want sparsity on correlated tabular data.

axes.note: cyclic coordinate descent is deterministic; selection='random' is the only stochastic mode

emits.note: POINT ESTIMATES ONLY — no SEs from sklearn; sparse-with-grouping support pattern is the effect story

l1_ratio.note: the L1/L2 mix; endpoints excluded — 1.0 IS lasso, and sklearn's own docs advise Ridge over coordinate descent at 0.0

invariances.why: both penalty components are unit-dependent — unscaled features get arbitrary relative shrinkage AND arbitrary selection thresholds
linear in the inputs; monotone transforms change fit and support
coordinate descent has no missing-value path; NaN raises
requires a pre-encoded numeric design matrix
squared-error loss presumes a linear mean; the mixed penalty bets the signal is sparse-but-grouped
defined at p >> n like lasso, but the L2 component removes lasso's at-most-n-features ceiling — the strictly safer wide-data choice
the linear predictor extends unboundedly beyond the training range

featureStats.why: the grouping effect is the point: the L2 term makes correlated features enter/exit the support together — high correlation is the commit-enet-over-lasso signal
wide data is home turf; unlike lasso, the support size is not capped at n thanks to the strictly convex L2 component
the same collinearity that destabilizes lasso's pick and inflates OLS variance is exactly what the L2 blend is dosed (via l1_ratio) to absorb

modelMetrics.why: on correlated designs enet's fold-to-fold support overlap should beat lasso's — if it doesn't, l1_ratio is set too close to 1 to buy the grouping effect
a boosted-tree model decisively winning says the residual signal is non-linear — sparsity tuning cannot close a functional-form gap

edgeCases.behavior: pure L2 objective solved by coordinate descent — sklearn's docs recommend Ridge's closed-form solvers instead
exactly lasso — the grouping effect vanishes
all coefficients zero; intercept-only model returned silently
coefficients from an unconverged pass; usually tiny alpha or unscaled X

driver.threadSafety: single-threaded coordinate descent; predict is thread-safe

placementClaims.why: no native NaN path — coordinate descent raises on missing values
linearizing skewed covariates improves the linear-mean fit the squared loss assumes
both penalty components are unit-dependent — standardization is what makes shrinkage and selection comparable across features
categoricals must be design-encoded; the grouping effect then usefully keeps one-hot siblings together
